body:
T-129 was a crash on the very first frame of the app, in code that had a green
test suite. The gap that let it through is structural, not a one-off oversight.

Every Compose UI test passes its view model in explicitly:

    ListScreen(viewModel = fakeViewModel, ...)

That was the right fix for T-127 (the screens render in a bare ComponentActivity
under Robolectric, where `hiltViewModel()` cannot work). But it means the
`viewModel: X = hiltViewModel()` DEFAULT — the path every real launch takes — is
executed by no test at all. T-129 broke exactly that default, for every screen at
once, and nothing went red.

The locale unit tests did not catch it either, because they asserted the thing
that still worked: `createConfigurationContext` resolves strings in the right
language perfectly well. It only broke the context CHAIN, which nothing asserted
until `LocalizedContextTest` was added.

Wanted: one smoke test that launches the real `MainActivity` through
`HiltAndroidRule` / `createAndroidComposeRule<MainActivity>()` and asserts the
first screen composes. It does not need to assert any behaviour — "the app
starts" is the entire point, and that single assertion would have failed loudly
on T-129.

Open question worth deciding first: whether this belongs in the Robolectric unit
suite (fast, runs in verify-all, but needs Hilt test wiring and a stand-in for
the server) or as an instrumented androidTest (realistic, but needs a device or
emulator and so would not run in verify-all on this machine). The Robolectric
route is the one that would actually gate a release here.

Not urgent — the specific bug is fixed and now has its own regression test. This
is about the class of bug.
title: Android: no test exercises the hiltViewModel() default — the path every real launch takes
